SETTING THE SCENE · 经济体制

What is an economic system?

An economic system = the set of:

• Institutions (rules & organizations)

• Mechanisms (processes)

that decide resource allocation & distribution

Two key differences between systems:

1. Who owns the resources?

2. Who decides what/how/for whom?

Four main types:

Traditional → Market → Command → Mixed

THE MARKET

What is a market?

A market is an arrangement which brings buyers into contact with sellers and which includes all the buyers and sellers 市场 = 把买卖双方带到一起、并涵盖所有买卖双方的安排<

A market does NOT need a shop building!

Where do markets exist?

• Local: the vegetable market, the school canteen · 菜市场、食堂

• Online: Taobao, Amazon — buyers & sellers never meet face to face

• Global: foreign exchange (FOREX), oil, stocks — traded worldwide 24 hours

In every market the two sides bargain and a price emerges.
The price is how a market communicates — no telephone lines needed.

THE MARKET · 市场的组成

What is a market made of?

BUYERS

consumers · the demand side

Who wants the good, and how much are they willing to pay?
买奶茶的你 —— 需求方

SELLERS

producers / firms · the supply side

Who makes the good, and at what cost?
喜茶店员 —— 供给方

Buyers and sellers each act for their own interest: consumers want low prices, producers want profit. No one is in charge of the other.

So what stops it descending into chaos?

The price coordinates them:

• If too few goods → price rises → more sellers attracted, buyers discouraged

• If too many goods → price falls → sellers sellers cut back, buyers encouraged

Price = the market’s invisible coordinator · 价格的协调作用

THE PRICE MECHANISM · 价格机制

How prices allocate scarce resources

Watch the loop: demand → price → signal → resources. Click Next stage · 点 Next 逐步看。
Press Next stage to begin.
THE PRICE MECHANISM · EXAM TERMS

Three jobs of the price mechanism

0455 exam vocabulary: how prices do three things at once.

① Signalling function · 信号功能

Prices carry information. A rising price says “scarce, produce more”; a falling price says “plenty, cut back”.

② Incentive function · 激励功能

High prices give producers an incentive to supply more (profit motive); low prices push them to be efficient or leave the market.

③ Rationing function · 价格配给（按价分配）

When a good is scarce, price decides who gets it: those willing and able to pay — i.e. the highest bidder. Not by need, not by fairness — by price 价格配给。

E.g. concert tickets, scarce housing, a hospital bed in a private system.

Exam sentence to memorise:

“The price mechanism allocates scarce resources through its signalling, incentive and rationing functions.”

BACK TO THE THREE QUESTIONS

How the market answers them

WHAT?

Whatever is profitable to sell. Popular goods keep being made; unwanted goods are discontinued.

HOW?

Producers compete on cost — inefficient firms are squeezed out. Lowest-cost methods survive.

FOR WHOM?

Whoever has the income and willingness to pay — the highest bidder gets the good.

No planner in charge — Adam Smith called it the “invisible hand” · 看不见的手

Consumers “vote” with their spending; prices count the votes and direct resources automatically.

WHO SAW IT FIRST? · 经济学之父

Adam Smith (1723–1790)

Adam Smith · 亚当·斯密

1723–1790, Scottish philosopher · 苏格兰人

1776 — The Wealth of Nations · 《国富论》: the first systematic book of economics.

We call him the father of economics · 经济学之父

His famous quote · 名言

“It is not from the benevolence of the butcher, the brewer, or the baker, that we expect our dinner, but from for their regard to their own interest.”

我们吃上晚餐，不是因为屠夫、酿酒师、面包师的仁慈，而是因为他们关心自己的利益。

Profile from a 1787 medallion by James Tassie · 詹姆斯·塔西 1787 徽章像

THE BIG DEBATE · 持续两个半世纪的争论

Is the market always right?

Economics was born with this question — it is still unanswered today.

FOR the market · 市场派

Adam Smith, 1776: self-interest + competition → efficiency. Leave markets alone (laissez-faire, 自由放任) and resources find their best use.

AGAINST trusting it fully · 质疑派

But markets are not perfect:
• Who cleans up pollution? Who builds roads?
• What if the poor cannot afford medicine?
• What if sellers cheat (fake reviews, lies)?

Economists have argued for 250 years about how much the government should interfere — and two giants became the faces of the two camps.

Meet them on the next page →

TWO GIANTS · 两位巨人

Marx & Keynes

Two answers to the big debate — and the two systems they inspired.

Karl Marx · 马克思

1818–1883 · 《资本论》Das Kapital

Exploitation (surplus value ) is built into capitalism; economic crises are inevitable under the market; capitalism will inevitably fall

The answer: public ownership + central planning

→ The idea behind planned economies

John Maynard Keynes · 凯恩斯

1883–1946 · 《通论》General Theory (1936)

In a crisis, markets can stay depressed for years — so government must spend to pull the economy out.

→ The idea behind mixed economies

Their debate is why today’s economies are mixed — market + government · 两种思想的平衡

ECONOMIC SYSTEMS

Type 1: Market economy / Capitalism

Also called capitalist or free-market economy

• Private ownership of resources

• Decentralized decisions by consumers & producers

• Price mechanism (supply & demand) coordinates

Key features:

• Consumer sovereignty: "voting with dollars"

• Profit motive → competition → efficiency

• Limited government: "laissez-faire"

"The invisible hand" — Adam Smith

ECONOMIC SYSTEMS

Type 2: Traditional economy

Based on customs, habits, traditions

Examples: remote villages in less developed regions

Key features:

• Occupations passed down parent → child

• Very slow change, little innovation

• Agriculture, hunting, fishing, gathering

• Barter, little trade

ECONOMIC SYSTEMS

Type 3: Command / Planned economy

Also called planned, socialist, or communist economy

• Public (state) ownership of resources

• Centralized decisions by the government

• Central planning authority sets targets, allocates resources

Key features:

• Planners, not consumers, answer the three questions

• Little consumer choice

Examples: former USSR, North Korea

💭 Thinker behind it · 思想源头: Karl Marx 马克思 (1818–1883)

ECONOMIC SYSTEMS

Type 4: Mixed economy

= a mix of market + command

• Private sector: private ownership, free markets

• Public sector: government provides public goods, regulates

Why mixed?

• Markets sometimes fail (pollution, public goods)

• Government can improve: defence, roads, schools, welfare

Almost all real-world economies are mixed.

e.g. USA, UK, China — different mixes

💭 Thinker behind it · 思想源头: John Maynard Keynes 凯恩斯 (1883–1946)

COMPARISON

Comparison: four economic systems

FINAL SUMMARY · 一条时间轴看四种体制

Economic systems through history

One timeline, four systems — where each came from, and where they all ended up. 一条时间轴：四种体制的来龙去脉。

EARLIEST · 最早

🏘️ Traditional

Customs decide everything; skills pass down generations. 习俗主导，代际传承，变化极慢。

1776 → · 工业革命时代

🏭 Market / Capitalism

Smith's Wealth of Nations + industrial revolution: prices & profit allocate resources.

1917 → · 对市场弊病的回应

🏛️ Command / Planned

Marx's ideas put into practice (USSR): state owns & plans · 公有制+中央计划。

LATE 1900s → today · 殊途同归

🤝 Mixed

BOTH sides moved: market economies added government (Keynes); planned economies added markets (China 1978, USSR 1991).

The timeline converges: whatever the starting point, almost every economy today is MIXED. 时间轴的终点几乎都是混合经济——两条路，殊途同归。
